issues.failure_explanation: In the proof of Theorem 4.1, the auxiliary function u_*^e is defined by u_*^e = \chi u^e \circ q_\delta, where q_\delta is the closest point projection onto the hypersurface \partial\Omega_\delta. Equation (48) asserts that \|u_*^e\|_{H^s} \lesssim \|u^e\|_{H^s} by standard multiplication and composition estimates. However, q_\delta is a projection onto a codimension 1 boundary, not a diffeomorphism. The function u^e \circ q_\delta is constant along normal rays, so its tangential derivatives of order s are the derivatives of the trace u^e|_{\partial\Omega_\delta}. By the trace theorem, for u^e \in H^s, the trace only belongs to H^{s - 1/2}(\partial\Omega_\delta). Hence, u^e \circ q_\delta does not belong to H^s(U_{\delta_2}(\partial\Omega_\delta)) in general, and its H^{p+1}-norm cannot be bounded by \|u\|_{H^{p+1}(\Omega)}. This invalidates the bounds on terms I_1, I_{2,1}, I_{2,2}, and I_{2,3}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the regularity assumption on the exact solution in Theorem 4.1 to u^e \in H^{p + 3/2}(U_{\delta_2}(\partial\Omega_\delta)) (or u \in H^{p+2}(\Omega)), ensuring by the trace theorem that u^e|_{\partial\Omega_\delta} \in H^{p+1}(\partial\Omega_\delta)$ and therefore \|u_*^e\|_{H^{p+1}} is controlled by the norm of u.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem 4.1 fails under the stated regularity assumption u \in H^{p+1}(\Omega). All bounds in the proof that estimate interpolation and stabilization errors of u_*^e by h^p \|u\|_{H^{p+1}(\Omega)} become unsupported.
issues.title: Invalid Sobolev norm estimate for composition with closest point projection
issues.why_classification: The error rates in h, \delta, and \delta_n survive, but the statement of Theorem 4.1 must be weakened to require higher Sobolev regularity on u than the standard bulk H^{p+1} assumption, leaving a recognizably comparable result without requiring a new overall proof architecture.
